bull.b: The 20-year power agreement provides a durable foundation for Phase 1 by addressing a critical input for data-center operations. Contracted capacity can improve project bankability, support tenant negotiations, and reduce exposure to future power availability constraints.

Full Phase 1 permitting and active site work indicate the project has moved beyond an early concept toward execution. This progress may shorten the path to operations, improve delivery visibility, and support conversion of the development pipeline into recurring infrastructure revenue.

The PIPE strengthens near-term financial capacity by repaying borrowings and preserving cash for development and leasing work. A cleaner balance sheet can improve negotiating flexibility with tenants and financing partners while supporting progress toward commercializing the project.

bear.b: The sharp revenue contraction and deeply negative profitability show that the current operating base is not yet supporting the business economically. Persistent cash consumption increases reliance on external funding and makes future earnings depend heavily on successful project execution.

Even with agreement on lease economics, the absence of a signed definitive contract leaves an important commercialization milestone incomplete. Delays in final scope, payment timing, or delivery responsibilities could postpone financing, construction commitments, and revenue realization.

Phase 2 capacity and the broader 757 MW plan remain dependent on regulatory approval that has not yet been received. A delayed permit could defer generation deployment, extend the development timetable, and reduce the pace at which the company can expand its planned campus.
